criterion_scores.reasoning: Mostly sound against the supplied decisions: the new pre-event gate is distinct, stage_research writes claims/documents without creating an event row, and attach_research later binds them on attendance. I checked the numbered decisions and the main code paths; the main issue I found is the overbroad correspondence filter in parse_ledger (line 295), which can wrongly skip valid claims, so this is good but not perfect.

The artifact covers the requested mechanics end-to-end: parser, gate verbs, freeze list, attach-on-attendance, and selftests. The main shortcoming is the Step 4.2d reporting format not matching the spec wording exactly (line 530), but the functional path is present and the acceptance flow is otherwise covered.

Placement and naming look consistent with the repo’s conventions: the new spec lives under .claude/notes, the command docs were updated, and the new verb is wired into substrate.py and the hook. I did not see a house-convention violation like an alex: prefix misuse or a parent/child-thread write-path breach.

The change stays lean and targeted: a parser, a gate split, and attachment logic rather than a new parallel pipeline. I looked for duplicated state or unnecessary ceremony and didn’t find a serious anti-pattern; the only concern is the overly permissive correspondence regex, which is more a correctness leak than an architecture smell.

Diagnostics are generally good: the new paths return explicit exit codes, the loud failure text says why zero rows is fatal, and the selftests cover the important cases. The only nit is that the Step 4.2d printout is less structured than the spec asks for, so the operator-facing message is slightly less legible than it could be.

defects.description: The correspondence detector is too broad: the alternation also matches the bare token `Alex`, so any legitimate claim text mentioning Alex will be classified as private correspondence and skipped. That can drop valid email-signal claims even when they have a public URL and are not correspondence.

defects.description: The success report format does not match the spec’s required Step 4.2d line shape (`Graph: <N> research claims (web <W> · email-lead <E>) · skipped <S> · unlinked headings <list or none>`). It reports a different prefix and omits the explicit web/email/skipped grouping the command text asks for.
